title: siRNA-mediated knockdown of target genes in RA-induced neurogenesis using P19 cells
author: Khodadadi, Taniguchi
materials: For neuronal differentiation, P19 cells were induced with 0.5 µM retinoic acid (RA) (Cat. #R2625; Sigma-Aldrich, St. Louis, MO, USA) in a differentiation medium (same components as the maintenance medium supplemented with 2 % FBS instead of the standard 10 %), for 4 days in a non-adherent culture dish (Cat. #633,180; Greiner bio-one GmbH, Kremsmünster, Austria) to promote the formation of embryoid bodies (EBs). Subsequently, EBs were plated onto adherent culture dishes and allowed to further differentiate in maintenance medium for an additional 6 days [1].

Lipofectamine™ RNAiMAX (Thermo Fisher Scientific, Cat. #13,778,075) and Optimem were used to transfect the siRNA of gene of interest (for our study we used mouse Nfe2l1 siRNA (siNfe2l1), Sense: GCCUGUAGAAGAAUUCAAU, Antisense: AUUGAAUUCUUCUACAGGC), and Negative Control siRNA (siNC) (MISSION® siRNA Universal Negative Control, Sigma-Aldrich, Cat. #SIC-001) to the cells.

•On day 10 of neurogenesis, using the NucleoSpin RNA Mini kit for RNA purification (MACHEREY-NAGEL, Cat. #740,955.50), the total RNA was isolated from all the Neuronal-like cells.•Next, we used 0.5 µg of total RNA to produce cDNA by the NG dART RT kit according to the manufacturer's instructions (EURx, Cat. #E0801).•RT-qPCR was performed to measure the expression levels of Map2 (neuronal marker), Pax6 (neuronal progenitor marker), Oct4 (pluripotency marker), and β-Actin (control gene). The reactions utilized SYBR Green Master Mix (Cat. #2017–100HS, A&A Biotechnology) on the Roche LightCyclerⓇ 480 System. The cycling conditions were as follows: an initial incubation at 95 °C for 5 min, followed by 40 cycles of 95 °C for 10 s, 60 °C for 10 s, and 72 °C for 10 s. Relative expression levels of target genes were normalized to β-Actin and analyzed using the 2^(-ΔΔCt) method. steps.title: Maintain P19 cells in T25 flask
steps.instruction: Culture P19 cells in a T25 flask (25 cm²) using maintenance medium composed of DMEM high glucose with stable glutamine and sodium pyruvate (Biowest, Cat. #L0130), supplemented with 10 % FBS, 100 U/mL penicillin and 100 U/mL streptomycin; incubate at 37 °C, 5 % CO₂.

steps.title: Induce embryoid body formation with RA
steps.instruction: Prepare differentiation medium identical to the maintenance medium but containing 2 % FBS instead of 10 %; add 0.5 µM retinoic acid (RA) (Sigma‑Aldrich, Cat. #R2625). Transfer P19 cells to a non‑adherent culture dish (Greiner, Cat. #633,180) and culture for 4 days to generate embryoid bodies (EBs).

steps.title: Plate embryoid bodies and continue differentiation
steps.instruction: After 4 days, plate the formed EBs onto standard adherent culture dishes and continue incubation in the original maintenance medium (10 % FBS) for an additional 6 days.

steps.title: Transfect cells with siRNA using RNAiMAX
steps.instruction: Use Lipofectamine™ RNAiMAX (Thermo Fisher Scientific, Cat. #13,778,075) together with Opti‑MEM to form complexes with either mouse Nfe2l1 siRNA (Sense: GCCUGUAGAAGAAUUCAAU; Antisense: AUUGAAUUCUUCUACAGGC) or Negative Control siRNA (MISSION® Universal Negative Control, Sigma‑Aldrich, Cat. #SIC-001). Add the complexes to the cells according to the manufacturer’s protocol.

steps.title: Isolate total RNA on day 10
steps.instruction: On day 10 of neurogenesis, harvest neuronal‑like cells and isolate total RNA using the NucleoSpin RNA Mini kit (MACHEREY‑NAGEL, Cat. #740,955.50) following the kit instructions.

steps.title: Synthesize cDNA and perform RT‑qPCR
steps.instruction: Take 0.5 µg of the isolated RNA and synthesize cDNA with the NG dART RT kit (EURx, Cat. #E0801) per the manufacturer’s protocol. Set up quantitative PCR reactions using SYBR Green Master Mix (A&A Biotechnology, Cat. #2017‑100HS) on a Roche LightCycler® 480. Use primers for Map2, Pax6, Oct4 and β‑Actin (sequences listed in Table 1). Cycling conditions: 95 °C 5 min; 40 cycles of 95 °C 10 s, 60 °C 10 s, 72 °C 10 s. Analyze relative expression by normalizing to β‑Actin and applying the 2⁻ΔΔCt method.
